earth_ice_free_land.definition: ice_free_land = land_mask AND NOT ice, where ice = (ETOPO 60s surface - ETOPO 60s bed) > 20 m. This is the step-3 Earth reference population: the land mask alone would include the Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets, so every Earth percentile would be computed over a population that is about a tenth ice.
earth_ice_free_land.resampling: ice mask upsampled 1/60 -> 1/240 by EXACT 4x NEAREST replication; it is a mask and is never interpolated
earth_ice_free_land.threshold_rationale: surface minus bed is a difference of two float32 rasters, so it is not exactly zero over bare rock: a few metres of noise and of genuine surface-versus-bedrock disagreement (sediment, water bodies, build-up) are expected. A threshold of exactly 0 would therefore classify noise as ice. Ice sheets are hundreds to thousands of metres thick, so any threshold between a few metres and a few tens of metres separates them from noise by two orders of magnitude. 20 m is chosen as the middle of that range; the area at 5, 20 and 50 m is reported so the insensitivity is visible rather than asserted.
earth_ice_free_land.nodata_rule: a cell is ice only where BOTH surface and bed are valid; where either is nodata the cell is not called ice

thickness.negative_note: surface < bed by more than 1 m should not happen; a nonzero count means the two products disagree somewhere and is reported rather than clipped away

scar_crosscheck.interpretation: outcrops are exposed rock, so a high percentage inside ice_free_land is confirmation. The ice mask is built at 1/60 deg (~1.85 km) while many outcrops are a few hundred metres across, so small ones sit in cells that are mostly ice and are expected to be classified ice. The agreement rate therefore measures the resolution limit of the ice mask, not whether the mask is correct. Vertices are tested rather than filled polygons, because no geometry library is installed -- a weaker test, and stated as such.

size_stratified.question: is the disagreement a resolution effect, or is the ice mask wrong?
size_stratified.method: per-feature bounding-box area from the GeoPackage R-tree index, centroid tested against ice_free_land, stratified by area. One 1/240 output cell is ~0.21 km2; the ice mask is derived at 1/60 deg, ~3.4 km2 per cell at Antarctic latitudes.
size_stratified.verdict: CONFIRMED RESOLUTION EFFECT: agreement rises monotonically with outcrop size, 19.2% for sub-cell features to 70.2% above 50 km2, and 65% of the 74,781 features are sub-cell. The ice mask is not wrong; it cannot resolve a nunatak.
size_stratified.but_also_a_real_limitation: area-weighted, only 49.8% of catalogued outcrop area survives into ice_free_land, so ANTARCTIC EXPOSED ROCK IS UNDER-REPRESENTED in the Earth reference population. This matters because the lunar targets are polar and Antarctica is the obvious terrestrial polar analog -- the same theme as earth_silica being only 2.24% valid above 85 deg.
size_stratified.option_not_taken: the SCAR polygons could be rasterised and unioned into ice_free_land to restore the missing outcrop. Not done here: no geometry library is installed, so polygon filling would have to be hand-rolled, and it is outside the Phase 1b specification. Recorded as a recommendation.

moon_slope.binning: area-weighted mean onto HEALPix NESTED with cos(lat) weights, accumulated INSIDE the band loop; no intermediate at working resolution was written
moon_slope.nodata_rule: NaN propagates from the DEM. A window statistic is NaN where under 50% of the window is valid; slope is NaN where either stencil end is NaN; H is NaN where any of the four scales is invalid or zero, or where R2 < 0.9

aggregation_decision.spec_says: median of the native values inside the HEALPix pixel
aggregation_decision.implemented: area-weighted mean, cos(lat) weights, accumulated inside the band loop
aggregation_decision.status: DEPARTURE FROM SPEC -- deliberate; the spec is to be updated
reasoning: A mean streams and a median does not. The mean needs two accumulators of length npix, 96 MB for the Moon and 201 MB for Earth, and a pixel never has to be complete within one band. A median needs every contributing value present at once, which means writing a working-resolution intermediate -- 13.9 GiB per Earth layer, about 97 GiB over the seven layers -- then reading it back.
Each HEALPix pixel averages roughly 215 native cells, so the sampling error on the mean is small.
All three DEMs passed their range and coverage gates in phase 1, so the outlier robustness a median buys has no known outliers to defend against.
The quantities being aggregated are smooth window statistics, already averaged over 5 to 42 km footprints, so within one 7 km pixel they vary little and mean and median nearly coincide.
aggregation_decision.consequence: Where a pixel straddles a sharp boundary -- a crater rim, a coastline -- the mean is pulled toward the extreme while a median would ignore it. The support gate is what exposes those pixels.

moon_slope.ew_saturation_note: The east-west stencil widens as 1/cos(lat) and is capped at half the parallel. A capped row measures a SHORTER extent than requested; ew_rows_saturated counts them.

support_gate.definition: achieved weight total over expected weight total: the cos(lat)-weighted fraction of the native cells falling in the pixel that carried a usable value
support_gate.thin_support_warning: A pixel passing the coverage gate on a small support fraction is a weak measurement, not a missing one. Filter on support, not on validity alone.

slope_parameters.gradient: hypot of the north-south and east-west differences

moon_slope.throughput_note: bytes_read divided by elapsed. This is a COMPUTE rate, not a disk rate: phase 2 reads the DEM once and then does far more work per byte than phase 1, which measured 156 MB/s on this same disk. Do not read it as I/O throughput.
moon_slope.ew_saturation_formula: total capped rows = window / (pi * cell_size). The body radius cancels completely: cell = pi*R/H, so extent*H/(pi^2*R) reduces to extent/(pi*cell). Because all three grids target 463-474 m cells by design, the identical counts of 4 / 8 / 14 / 28 rows for the 5.25 / 10.5 / 21 / 42 km windows are FORCED, not a coincidence. Predicted 3.53/7.05/14.11/28.22 (moon) and 3.61/7.21/14.43/28.86 (mars, earth); observed counts agree to +/-1 row, the residual being the rounding of a fractional threshold row.

validation.fit: OLS of log(sigma) on CENTRED log(achieved scale)
validation.estimator_note: Moving-window standard deviation at four scales, NOT Shepard's deviogram. The name is roughness_scaling_exponent rather than 'hurst' for exactly that reason: the estimator differs from the one the Hurst literature assumes, so these numbers are not interchangeable with published H values.
validation.validated_on: synthetic fractional Brownian surfaces at H = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 using this body's achieved scales; see the fBm gate in the Phase 2 report
validation.outside_unit_interval: Values below 0 and above 1 are NOT errors. This is the slope of log roughness against log scale, which may legitimately exceed 1: it does so where a widening window swallows a discrete feature such as a crater rim and roughness grows faster than linearly. Those pixels are detecting DISCRETE FEATURES rather than fractal texture -- a real measurement of the wrong quantity. A value below 0 says roughness FALLS as the window widens. R2 does not screen either case out, because the power law is clean; only its exponent is meaningless as a texture descriptor. This is also why the layer is named roughness_scaling_exponent and not hurst.
validation.redundancy_finding: VARIABLES.md section B8 predicted HIGH redundancy against ruggedness. That prediction is WRONG. Measured correlation of this layer with roughness_21km on the Moon is -0.157 globally and -0.306 over 85-90S. H carries information nothing else carries; it is simply noisy. The B8 verdict of HOLD stands, but for the signal-to-noise reason, not the redundancy reason.
validation.status: HOLD -- built and stored, not wired into the default dimension set

validation.validated_on: synthetic fractional Brownian surfaces at H = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 using this body's achieved scales; see the fBm gate in the Phase 2 report
validation.outside_unit_interval: Values below 0 and above 1 are NOT errors. This is the slope of log roughness against log scale, which may legitimately exceed 1: it does so where a widening window swallows a discrete feature such as a crater rim and roughness grows faster than linearly. Those pixels are detecting DISCRETE FEATURES rather than fractal texture -- a real measurement of the wrong quantity. A value below 0 says roughness FALLS as the window widens. R2 does not screen either case out, because the power law is clean; only its exponent is meaningless as a texture descriptor. This is also why the layer is named roughness_scaling_exponent and not hurst.
validation.redundancy_finding: VARIABLES.md section B8 predicted HIGH redundancy against ruggedness. That prediction is WRONG. Measured correlation of this layer with roughness_21km on the Moon is -0.157 globally and -0.306 over 85-90S. H carries information nothing else carries; it is simply noisy. The B8 verdict of HOLD stands, but for the signal-to-noise reason, not the redundancy reason.

aggregation_decision.spec_says: median of the native values inside the HEALPix pixel
aggregation_decision.implemented: area-weighted mean, cos(lat) weights, accumulated inside the band loop
aggregation_decision.status: DEPARTURE FROM SPEC -- deliberate; the spec is to be updated
reasoning: A mean streams and a median does not. The mean needs two accumulators of length npix, 96 MB for the Moon and 201 MB for Earth, and a pixel never has to be complete within one band. A median needs every contributing value present at once, which means writing a working-resolution intermediate -- 13.9 GiB per Earth layer, about 97 GiB over the seven layers -- then reading it back.
Each HEALPix pixel averages roughly 215 native cells, so the sampling error on the mean is small.
All three DEMs passed their range and coverage gates in phase 1, so the outlier robustness a median buys has no known outliers to defend against.
The quantities being aggregated are smooth window statistics, already averaged over 5 to 42 km footprints, so within one 7 km pixel they vary little and mean and median nearly coincide.
aggregation_decision.consequence: Where a pixel straddles a sharp boundary -- a crater rim, a coastline -- the mean is pulled toward the extreme while a median would ignore it. The support gate is what exposes those pixels.

mars_scaling_exponent_r2.gates: THREE gates, not two: range (are the values plausible), coverage (did the pixel get anything) and support (how much of the pixel actually contributed). The coverage gate alone lies: a pixel reports valid while resting on a handful of its ~215 contributing cells.
mars_scaling_exponent_r2.slope_convention: slope uses CENTRE-TO-CENTRE spacing, 2*h*cell: a slope is a height difference ACROSS a distance, so only the two endpoints and their separation enter. 7 km requested -> 7.58 km achieved at 463 m.
mars_scaling_exponent_r2.window_convention: window statistics use the FULL FOOTPRINT, (2*h+1)*cell: a window statistic covers an AREA, so the centre cell counts. 21 km requested -> 20.85 km achieved at 463 m.
mars_scaling_exponent_r2.convention_warning: These two conventions differ BY DESIGN and must not be reconciled. A later reader who 'fixes' one to match the other will silently change every terrain variable.
mars_scaling_exponent_r2.tpi_sign_convention: TPI = z - mean(z within the window). TPI < 0 means the cell is LOWER than its surroundings, i.e. INSIDE A BOWL (crater floor, basin, valley). TPI > 0 means a rim, ridge or peak.
mars_scaling_exponent_r2.ew_saturation_note: The east-west stencil widens as 1/cos(lat) and is capped at half the parallel. A capped row measures a SHORTER extent than requested; ew_rows_saturated counts them.

validation.fit: OLS of log(sigma) on CENTRED log(achieved scale)
validation.estimator_note: Moving-window standard deviation at four scales, NOT Shepard's deviogram. The name is roughness_scaling_exponent rather than 'hurst' for exactly that reason: the estimator differs from the one the Hurst literature assumes, so these numbers are not interchangeable with published H values.
validation.validated_on: synthetic fractional Brownian surfaces at H = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 using this body's achieved scales; see the fBm gate in the Phase 2 report
validation.outside_unit_interval: Values below 0 and above 1 are NOT errors. This is the slope of log roughness against log scale, which may legitimately exceed 1: it does so where a widening window swallows a discrete feature such as a crater rim and roughness grows faster than linearly. Those pixels are detecting DISCRETE FEATURES rather than fractal texture -- a real measurement of the wrong quantity. A value below 0 says roughness FALLS as the window widens. R2 does not screen either case out, because the power law is clean; only its exponent is meaningless as a texture descriptor. This is also why the layer is named roughness_scaling_exponent and not hurst.
validation.redundancy_finding: VARIABLES.md section B8 predicted HIGH redundancy against ruggedness. That prediction is WRONG. Measured correlation of this layer with roughness_21km on the Moon is -0.157 globally and -0.306 over 85-90S. H carries information nothing else carries; it is simply noisy. The B8 verdict of HOLD stands, but for the signal-to-noise reason, not the redundancy reason.

validation.temp_level_definition: (tbol_max + tbol_min)/2. This is a MIDPOINT, not a true full-cycle time average: the GCP's local-time sampling is uneven, and the lunar diurnal curve is strongly non-sinusoidal (long cold night, sharp noon peak), so the midpoint sits ABOVE the true time average. Stated rather than hidden; it is monotonic in the true average, which is what a rank transform needs.
validation.no_seasonal: The Moon has no meaningful seasonal cycle (axial tilt 1.54 deg), so temp_range_seasonal is NOT built for the Moon and must not enter the Earth-Moon dimension set.
validation.sampling_bias_checked: corr(n_local_time, |lat|) = +0.856: the POLES are the best sampled, median 96 of 96 bins at 85-90S against 55 at the equator. Within 2-degree latitude bands the correlation of n_local_time with diurnal range is -0.028, the effect is not monotonic in sampling, and max and min do NOT move in opposite directions. Bias bounded at ~0.3 K against a 265 K median range. No correction applied, and none is warranted.
validation.resampling_note: BIN THEN FILL. Pixels whose footprint contained at least one source cell carry an area-weighted MEAN of those cells. Pixels with no source cell carry a nearest-neighbour COPY and are marked by SUPPORT EXACTLY 0.0 ALONGSIDE A FINITE VALUE -- that combination means copied, not missing. A plate carree source is not uniformly coarse: a 0.5 degree cell is 15.2 km north-south but 15.2*cos(lat) km east-west, so the same source is finer than the pixel near the poles and coarser near the equator. Copying everywhere would have thrown away real polar detail in the lunar target region; binning everywhere would have left most of the sphere empty, which the coverage gate caught at 28.88% valid.
validation.tie_note: distinct_levels and largest_tie_fraction are the FOURTH gate. Copied pixels make neighbours carry identical values, and range, coverage and support are all blind to that.

validation.diurnal_definition_shared: DIURNAL RANGE IS DEFINED IDENTICALLY ON ALL THREE BODIES: max minus min over the AVAILABLE LOCAL TIMES. The limitation is a stated SAMPLE COUNT, not a different physical quantity. Earth 4 local times (Terra day/night + Aqua day/night), Mars 12, Moon 96. Because it is max minus min it is non-negative by construction on every body; the earlier Earth two-sample day-minus-night could and did go negative.

mars_temp_level.status: MODELLED, NOT MEASURED. Computed with a one-dimensional surface heat-balance model (NumPy port of KRC one-point mode, Kieffer 2013, validated against KRC's reference set to a median 1.4 K) driven by TES thermal inertia (Putzig & Mellon 2007), TES albedo (Christensen 2001), MOLA-derived surface pressure, latitude and the Montabone et al. (2015) dust climatology (MY29-MY32). No spacecraft measured a gridded surface-temperature climatology at this resolution. Expected error: a few kelvin in the mean, larger in the diurnal range and near the seasonal CO2 caps. Agreement with the Mars Climate Database was checked only at its 5.6 x 3.75 deg grid; the MCD high-resolution mode does not adjust surface temperature.

validation.diurnal_definition: max minus min over the AVAILABLE LOCAL TIMES -- the SAME quantity the Moon and Mars carry. Sample counts: Earth 4, Mars 12, Moon 96. validation.overpass_times: Terra ~10:30/22:30, Aqua ~13:30/01:30 local. These are MISSION DESIGN. The products' own view-time fields do not reproduce them when read: the distributions come out near-uniform over 0-24 h and Terra 'night' lands at 14.4 h. Two hypotheses were tested and REJECTED -- a 0.1 scale factor (caps at 12 h, cannot hold a night overpass) and swapped day/night bands (gives 14.4/9.0, still wrong). The times are therefore not claimed as measured, and nothing here depends on them: four distinct samples is all max-minus-min needs.
validation.cross_platform: Terra and Aqua are different instruments with independent calibration drift. For a rank transform computed WITHIN Earth this is negligible, because a common offset cannot change an ordering. Stated rather than assumed away.
validation.record_cost: ONE calendar year. A single anomalous season -- an El Nino, a volcanic aerosol loading, an unusual monsoon -- is not averaged out at all. The 22-month Terra record was longer, but the platforms did not line up, and consistency was the defect worth fixing.
validation.coverage_note: MOD11C3 and MYD11C3 are LAND ONLY and gap in polar night, so coverage varies by month. n_months is carried as the support value.
validation.resampling_note: BIN THEN FILL. Pixels whose footprint contained at least one source cell carry an area-weighted MEAN of those cells. Pixels with no source cell carry a nearest-neighbour COPY and are marked by SUPPORT EXACTLY 0.0 ALONGSIDE A FINITE VALUE -- that combination means copied, not missing. A plate carree source is not uniformly coarse: a 0.5 degree cell is 15.2 km north-south but 15.2*cos(lat) km east-west, so the same source is finer than the pixel near the poles and coarser near the equator. Copying everywhere would have thrown away real polar detail in the lunar target region; binning everywhere would have left most of the sphere empty, which the coverage gate caught at 28.88% valid.
validation.tie_note: distinct_levels and largest_tie_fraction are the FOURTH gate. Copied pixels make neighbours carry identical values, and range, coverage and support are all blind to that.

moon_SiO2.source: PDS lp-l-grs-5-elem-abundance-v1, lpgrs_high1_elem_abundance_2deg.tab; Prettyman et al. (2006)
moon_SiO2.source_unit: weight fraction g/g, converted to wt% by x100
moon_SiO2.uncertainty: per-cell, from the square root of the diagonal of the published 45-element error matrix; index 2 is SiO2, index 5 is FeO
moon_SiO2.resampling: exact point-in-cell assignment. LP cells and HEALPix pixels are BOTH equal-area, so no area weighting and no projection distortion. The source is coarser EVERYWHERE (~61 km cell against a 6.95 km pixel, ~70 pixels per cell), so every pixel is COPIED_FROM_COARSER.
moon_SiO2.why_lp_grs_not_diviner_cf: NOT because the Diviner CF map is unavailable -- it exists: Lucey et al. (2021, doi 10.1029/2020JE006777) derived a global lunar SiO2 map from the Christiansen Feature, +/-3.4 wt%. LP GRS was chosen because it gives BOTH oxides from one instrument on one grid WITH a published per-cell error matrix; the CF map is SiO2 only.
moon_SiO2.weak_dimension_moon: WEAK DIMENSION, MOON SIDE: across the 85-90S target region the lunar counterpart takes only 24 distinct values over ~1,512 HEALPix pixels, ~63 pixels per value, SiO2 spread 4.79 wt% (10.4% of global). Against a median per-cell sigma of 1.416 wt% that is only ~3.4 EFFECTIVELY SEPARABLE levels for SiO2 and ~5.1 for FeO. It acts as a near-fixed offset pointing Earth matches at mafic terrain, NOT as a discriminator between lunar targets.
moon_SiO2.weak_dimension_earth: WEAK DIMENSION, EARTH SIDE: the Earth counterpart is derived from GLiM, whose published ground truth is 40% of independent rock points matching the mapped class exactly and 64% allowing similar lithologies (Hartmann & Moosdorf 2012). That is the ceiling on any composition comparison using this pair.

earth_koppen_class.units: Koppen-Geiger class code, uint8, 1..30; 0 = no class
earth_koppen_class.source: Beck et al. (2023) Scientific Data 10, 724, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02549-6; 1991-2020 observational period, 30 arc-second GeoTIFF, uint8
earth_koppen_class.binning: MAJORITY VOTE, cos(lat)-weighted, per (pixel, class) pairs reduced band by band; the winning class is stored and its share is the support. The source is finer than the pixel everywhere, so every classified pixel is BINNED and none is copied.
earth_koppen_class.matching_eligible_reason: PERMANENT. A variable is a dimension only if both bodies in the pair have it, and the Moon and Mars have no Koppen class. This layer describes a site after it is found (step 9) and must never be wired into a dimension set.
earth_koppen_class.gates: FOUR: range (codes 1..30, stated in advance), coverage (global, by latitude band, and within the reference population), support (winning share) and ties (distinct_levels, largest_tie_fraction -- categorical, large ties expected).
earth_koppen_class.support_warning: support here is the winning class share, never 0.0 on a classified pixel. Read provenance_file for usability: 1 = BINNED, 3 = NO_VALID_SOURCE (the product covers the pixel but assigns no class, i.e. ocean), 0 = ABSENT.

classified_fraction.definition: share of the pixel's cos(lat)-weighted source cells that carry ANY class -- a land fraction by this product's own footprint; it is the coverage gate per pixel

support_gate.definition: winning class share of the pixel's cos(lat)-weighted classified cells; 1.0 means every classified source cell in the pixel agrees

reference_population.without_class_note: reference pixels the Koppen footprint does not reach: coastline and island differences between the 0.93 km Koppen land footprint and the WorldClim-derived land mask. Step 9 reports 'no class' for these, it does not guess one.

earth_reference_mask.units: fraction of the pixel's area that is reference land (0..1)
earth_reference_mask.derivation: TWO RULES. North of 60 S: cos(lat)-weighted area average of the 1/240 deg boolean earth_land_reference (land AND NOT ice AND NOT water bodies), by the same HealpixAccumulator every continuous layer uses. South of 60 S: the exposed rock + moraine share of the pixel measured by SCAR GeoMAP (Cox et al. 2023, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.951482), because the ice-thickness rule is wrong there in both directions (B31e).
earth_reference_mask.membership_rule: a pixel belongs to Earth's reference population where fraction > 0.5. This is the population the percentile transform (step 3) and the covariance (step 4) are computed over. Used by phase4a.

moon_tpi_7km.binning: area-weighted mean onto HEALPix NESTED with cos(lat) weights, accumulated INSIDE the band loop; no intermediate at working resolution was written
moon_tpi_7km.nodata_rule: NaN propagates from the DEM. A window statistic is NaN where under 50% of the window is valid; slope is NaN where either stencil end is NaN; H is NaN where any of the four scales is invalid or zero, or where R2 < 0.9

aggregation_decision.spec_says: median of the native values inside the HEALPix pixel
aggregation_decision.implemented: area-weighted mean, cos(lat) weights, accumulated inside the band loop
aggregation_decision.status: DEPARTURE FROM SPEC -- deliberate; the spec is to be updated
reasoning: A mean streams and a median does not. The mean needs two accumulators of length npix, 96 MB for the Moon and 201 MB for Earth, and a pixel never has to be complete within one band. A median needs every contributing value present at once, which means writing a working-resolution intermediate -- 13.9 GiB per Earth layer, about 97 GiB over the seven layers -- then reading it back.
Each HEALPix pixel averages roughly 215 native cells, so the sampling error on the mean is small.
All three DEMs passed their range and coverage gates in phase 1, so the outlier robustness a median buys has no known outliers to defend against.
The quantities being aggregated are smooth window statistics, already averaged over 5 to 42 km footprints, so within one 7 km pixel they vary little and mean and median nearly coincide.
aggregation_decision.consequence: Where a pixel straddles a sharp boundary -- a crater rim, a coastline -- the mean is pulled toward the extreme while a median would ignore it. The support gate is what exposes those pixels.

moon_tpi_7km.gates: THREE gates, not two: range (are the values plausible), coverage (did the pixel get anything) and support (how much of the pixel actually contributed). The coverage gate alone lies: a pixel reports valid while resting on a handful of its ~215 contributing cells.
moon_tpi_7km.slope_convention: slope uses CENTRE-TO-CENTRE spacing, 2*h*cell: a slope is a height difference ACROSS a distance, so only the two endpoints and their separation enter. 7 km requested -> 7.58 km achieved at 463 m.
moon_tpi_7km.window_convention: window statistics use the FULL FOOTPRINT, (2*h+1)*cell: a window statistic covers an AREA, so the centre cell counts. 21 km requested -> 20.85 km achieved at 463 m.
moon_tpi_7km.convention_warning: These two conventions differ BY DESIGN and must not be reconciled. A later reader who 'fixes' one to match the other will silently change every terrain variable.
moon_tpi_7km.tpi_sign_convention: TPI = z - mean(z within the window). TPI < 0 means the cell is LOWER than its surroundings, i.e. INSIDE A BOWL (crater floor, basin, valley). TPI > 0 means a rim, ridge or peak.
moon_tpi_7km.ew_saturation_note: The east-west stencil widens as 1/cos(lat) and is capped at half the parallel. A capped row measures a SHORTER extent than requested; ew_rows_saturated counts them.
moon_tpi_7km.ew_saturation_formula: total capped rows = window / (pi * cell_size). The body radius cancels completely: cell = pi*R/H, so extent*H/(pi^2*R) reduces to extent/(pi*cell). Because all three grids target 463-474 m cells by design, the identical counts of 4 / 8 / 14 / 28 rows for the 5.25 / 10.5 / 21 / 42 km windows are FORCED, not a coincidence. Predicted 3.53/7.05/14.11/28.22 (moon) and 3.61/7.21/14.43/28.86 (mars, earth); observed counts agree to +/-1 row, the residual being the rounding of a fractional threshold row.
moon_tpi_7km.shares_window_with: slope (7 km baseline); tpi_21km shares its window with roughness_21km
moon_tpi_7km.relation_to_tpi_21km: Same quantity, same code path (phase2_terrain.sat3 and window_stats_from_sat with want_mean=True), different window. TPI is strongly scale-dependent: 7 km separates small craters and rille floors that the 21 km window averages away; 21 km reads Shackleton-scale basins. Two radii give a crude landform decomposition for one extra pass (VARIABLES.md B1).

The option itself is B1's secondary recommendation. Built by build/phase2b_tpi7.py through phase 2's own functions; see VARIABLES.md B26 for the measurements.

moon_svf_30km.formula: SVF = 1 - (1/16) * sum_i sin(max(gamma_i, 0)); gamma_i = horizon elevation angle in azimuth i over a 30 km search radius. Zaksek, Ostir & Pokrajac (2011) Remote Sensing 3(2):398-415; horizon after Dozier, Bruno & Downey (1981). NOT the cosine-weighted Dozier & Frew (1990) form -- this layer is OPENNESS, the thermal layers carry radiation.
moon_svf_30km.computed_on: 2x2 block mean of the working DEM = 0.9476 km (B2: 'compute at 1 km'). Sub-kilometre terrain is invisible to this SVF; it measures basin-scale openness.
moon_svf_30km.polar_method: |lat| <= 80: plate carree band loop, column step scaled by 1/cos(lat) at the band centre so azimuths stay 22.5 deg apart, longitude wraps. |lat| > 80: polar stereographic caps on both poles (rasterio reproject, area-averaging resampler, 0.948 km square cells), the SAME kernel with cos = 1 and NaN padding, binned to HEALPix with true-area weights 1/k^2. A lat/lon sweep at the pole is wrong, not imprecise (B2, Appendix H).
moon_svf_30km.horizon_rule: angles compared, never elevations; a NaN neighbour is no obstruction (np.fmax); a NaN cell is NaN; horizon angle floored at 0
approximations: cos(lat) for the column step is taken at the band centre; a 256-row band spans 8.00 deg of latitude, so the azimuth error is under 2 deg at 80 deg lat
the 16 ray directions are rounded to whole cells per step, so the sampled azimuth wobbles by up to atan(0.5/k) at step k
the two passes share HEALPix pixels only where a pixel straddles 80 deg; there each pass contributes the cells on its side
moon_svf_30km.binning: area-weighted mean onto HEALPix NESTED: cos(lat) weights on the lat/lon pass, 1/k^2 stereographic-area weights on the caps, accumulated in one HealpixAccumulator
moon_svf_30km.gates: THREE: range (0..1, stated in advance), coverage, support.

earth_svf_30km.formula: SVF = 1 - (1/16) * sum_i sin(max(gamma_i, 0)); gamma_i = horizon elevation angle in azimuth i over a 30 km search radius. Zaksek, Ostir & Pokrajac (2011) Remote Sensing 3(2):398-415; horizon after Dozier, Bruno & Downey (1981). NOT the cosine-weighted Dozier & Frew (1990) form -- this layer is OPENNESS, the thermal layers carry radiation.
earth_svf_30km.computed_on: 2x2 block mean of the working DEM = 0.9266 km (B2: 'compute at 1 km'). Sub-kilometre terrain is invisible to this SVF; it measures basin-scale openness.
earth_svf_30km.polar_method: |lat| <= 80: plate carree band loop, column step scaled by 1/cos(lat) at the band centre so azimuths stay 22.5 deg apart, longitude wraps. |lat| > 80: polar stereographic caps on both poles (rasterio reproject, area-averaging resampler, 0.927 km square cells), the SAME kernel with cos = 1 and NaN padding, binned to HEALPix with true-area weights 1/k^2. A lat/lon sweep at the pole is wrong, not imprecise (B2, Appendix H).
earth_svf_30km.horizon_rule: angles compared, never elevations; a NaN neighbour is no obstruction (np.fmax); a NaN cell is NaN; horizon angle floored at 0
earth_svf_30km.earth_sea_rule: Earth only: cells outside earth_land_mask set to 0 m (the sea surface) before the sweep, because ETOPO carries bathymetry and a coast looks at the sea, not the seafloor. Inland water keeps its DEM value.
approximations: cos(lat) for the column step is taken at the band centre; a 256-row band spans 2.13 deg of latitude, so the azimuth error is under 2 deg at 80 deg lat
the 16 ray directions are rounded to whole cells per step, so the sampled azimuth wobbles by up to atan(0.5/k) at step k
the two passes share HEALPix pixels only where a pixel straddles 80 deg; there each pass contributes the cells on its side
earth_svf_30km.binning: area-weighted mean onto HEALPix NESTED: cos(lat) weights on the lat/lon pass, 1/k^2 stereographic-area weights on the caps, accumulated in one HealpixAccumulator
earth_svf_30km.gates: THREE: range (0..1, stated in advance), coverage, support.
earth_svf_30km.decision: Added 9 Nov 2026 on Sherozbek's decision: the Mars-Earth set was six elevation-derived variables and he asked for sky view factor on all three bodies as the form/openness dimension B2 specified. Built by build/phase2c_svf.py; measurements in VARIABLES.md B27.

earth_thermal_inertia.quantity_caveat: PROXY. Apparent thermal inertia is a dimensionless ratio of albedo to diurnal temperature swing; true thermal inertia needs a thermal model of the solar forcing, which is what the Mars partner (TES, Putzig & Mellon 2007) has. The pairing compares WHERE each body is thermally sluggish through the rank transform, not the physical value. B23 declined this pairing as a quantity mismatch; the 9 Nov 2026 decision overrides it and the mismatch is stated here and on mars_thermal_inertia.
earth_thermal_inertia.partial_record: BUILT FROM 10 ALBEDO MONTHS (Jan-May, Aug-Dec 2025). June and July cannot be exported from Google Earth Engine (Antarctic polar night leaves empty tiles, HANDOVER section 5 item 13). ACCEPTED AS FINAL by Sherozbek, 9 Nov 2026 (VARIABLES.md B29 addendum). The annual mean albedo therefore under-weights northern summer; the effect on a rank transform is small because albedo contributes little to ATI's ordering (rho with the diurnal range is -0.96).
